root.name: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Leningrad Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Bg5

overview: White pins the f6 knight at once with 4.Bg5. Black chooses between 4...h6 5.Bh4 (then ...c5 or ...g5 breaks), 4...c5, and 4...O-O. In the main lines Black gives up the bishop pair on c3, getting doubled c-pawns for White, or White keeps tension and develops quickly. The game is a manoeuvring fight for central control with some sharp options such as ...g5.

white_ideas.idea: Pin the knight, play e3, Qc2 or Qb3, and keep the bishop pair.
Meet ...c5 with d5 or dxc5 and use the pin.

black_ideas.idea: Break the pin with ...h6 and ...g5 or ...Bxc3+, and hit the centre with ...c5.
Double White's pawns with ...Bxc3+ and play against the weak c-pawns, with ...d6 and ...e5.

typical_structures.structure: White doubled c-pawns after bxc3 with the bishop pair against Black's central play.
After ...c5 d5 Black gets a Benoni-style asymmetric centre.

character.notes: Known for double-edged but strategic play; the sharp ...g5 lines exist, but most games are manoeuvring over doubled pawns and the pin.

gambit.notes: No pawn is sacrificed in the main lines.

soundness.notes: A main-line sound system for both sides.

structure.notes: Centre in tension with d4/c4 versus e6/c5; the pin and doubled pawns decide it.

approach.notes: A mainstream branch of the Nimzo-Indian.

level.notes: Pawn-structure play and a fair amount of theory; understanding of doubled pawns and bishop pair matters.

sublines_that_differ.name: Spielmann ...g5
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Bg5 h6 5. Bh4 g5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black attacks the bishop at once; the game becomes sharp with ...Ne4 and opposite attacking ideas.

character.reason: Strategic battle over doubled pawns and the bishop pair, with the sharp ...g5 branch rarer.

soundness.reason: A standard Nimzo line used at the top level.

structure.reason: Centre held in tension by the pin; d4/c4 against ...e6 and ...c5 undecided.

approach.reason: A mainstream branch of the Nimzo-Indian.

level.reason: Needs knowledge of the doubled pawn structures but not very long forcing lines.

plans.reason: Typical Nimzo trade-off of bishop pair against doubled pawns.
